title: Risk-aligned security messaging for AEs
text:
Risk-aligned security messaging for AEs

elevator_pitches:
For teams focused on speed-to-market: we operate a SOC2-ready hosted API with token-level observability and configurable data retention—fast onboarding, low friction.
For security-sensitive customers: Dedicated capacity gives you predictable throughput + network isolation and clear audit trails for compliance evidence.
For regulated or air-gapped needs: Redwood Private offers a VPC/on-prem control plane with KMS/HSM integrations and audit log exports tailored for HIPAA and ISO audits.

customer_risk_profiles:
We recommend AEs lead with different points depending on the customer's risk posture. Quick segmentation: 
- Risk Tier 1 (Startup/PLG): low contract friction, cares about quick POC and transparent pricing. Messaging: SOC2-in-progress or SOC2-ready hosted API, token-level cost visibility, safe defaults.
- Risk Tier 2 (Mid-market / Security-conscious): needs contractual assurances, SSO, encryption-in-transit+at-rest, audit logs export. Messaging: Dedicated preview, SLA options, log exports, ISO guidance. Offer to start with hosted and commit to dedicated at usage threshold.
- Risk Tier 3 (Regulated / Enterprise - HIPAA, FINRA, healthcare): requires contractual BAAs, private network, customer-managed KMS/HSM, long retention and e-discovery. Messaging: Redwood Private, on-prem option, support for compliance artifacts (SOC2 report, ISO attestation), hands-on onboarding from Solutions Engineering.

audit_log_language:
Draft audit-log snippet for contracts and security questionnaires: Redwood provides immutable, time-stamped audit logs for control plane and data-plane events. Logs capture request IDs, model and route used, token counts, requester identity (API key or customer identity provider subject), region, and response latency. Customers on Dedicated and Private can configure log retention and export to customer-owned S3 or SIEM via syslog/HTTPS. For HIPAA customers, logs can be exported to a customer-managed archive with encryption-at-rest (KMS) and role-based access controls. Typical retention options: 90 days (default), 1 year, and custom contractual retention for enterprise engagements.

positioning_golden_threads:
Short phrases AEs should weave into conversations: 
- 'Audit-first inference runtime'
- 'Unifies developer UX with enterprise guardrails'
- 'Deterministic fallbacks and observable decisions'
- 'Exportable, immutable audit trails for your auditors'
- 'Private deployments without rebuilding your stack'

ae_objection_responses:
Objection: 'We need a BAA before any integration.' -> Response: We support BAAs for production contracts and can provide HIPAA-ready deployment patterns via Redwood Private. Start with a scoped pilot under a narrow BAA if needed.
Objection: 'We can self-host to avoid audit risk.' -> Response: Self-hosting reduces vendor risk but increases operational and inference-cost risk. Redwood gives a middle path: private deployments with a Redwood control plane option, and we partner on runbooks/testing to produce audit evidence faster.
Objection: 'Audit logs are noisy / incomplete.' -> Response: We capture request-level telemetry (request ID, API key, route, model variant, token counts, timestamp, region) and provide configurable export hooks to your SIEM. We can also run a short proof to map your logging requirements to our fields.
Objection: 'What if we need data residency?' -> Response: We support region pinning on hosted for major regions, Dedicated pools in selected cloud regions, and Private deployments for strict residency. Combine with KMS and VPC controls for full compliance.

competitive_notes:
OpenAI / Large public APIs: Strength = breadth of models and simple sign-up. Weakness = less explicit enterprise isolation (unless using dedicated plans) and limited turnkey audit-export contracts. Positioning: emphasize Redwood's routing and deterministic fallbacks plus dedicated/private options.
Managed cloud vendors: Strength = deep security controls from cloud providers. Weakness = customers still manage model serving complexity and may lack inference-focused ops. Positioning: Redwood provides inference-optimized runtime + packaged compliance features (audit logs, KMS integrations) out of the box.
Self-hosted runtimes (vendors + OSS): Strength = control. Weakness = ops burden and inconsistent SRE maturity. Positioning: Redwood reduces time-to-prod with hardened runtime, observability, and curated guidance for SOC2/HIPAA readiness.
Inference specialists: Strength = performance focus. Weakness = poorer developer UX and inconsistent enterprise packaging. Positioning: call out unified API + rollout controls + auditability as enterprise differentiators.

audit_prep_checklist:
High-level checklist for AE + Solutions to prepare an audit-ready POC: 
1) Scope & Data Flow: Document which routes and models will process PHI/PII.
2) Deployment Mode: Choose Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Note contractual needs (BAA, region).
3) Logging & Retention: Configure audit log exports and retention. Confirm export location (customer S3 / SIEM).
4) Keys & Encryption: Plan KMS/HSM integration and key rotation policy.
5) Access Controls: Ensure RBAC + SSO mapping to customer identity providers.
6) Evidence Package: Pull together system diagrams, access logs, change control records, and SOC2/ISO artifacts.
7) Run Pilot: 2–4 week pilot with traffic that mirrors production and produce sample evidence for auditor.

—Priya
